acceptance_criteria.criterion: ClearableStringParameter class exists in Type/, extends StringParameter, and its resolveValue() returns null when the parameter key is absent from $_REQUEST.
resolveValue() returns '' (empty string) when the parameter key is present in $_REQUEST with an empty string or whitespace-only value (after trimming).
resolveValue() returns the trimmed string when the parameter key is present in $_REQUEST with a non-empty, non-whitespace-only value.

hasValue() (inherited from BaseAPIParameter) returns false when the parameter is absent, and true when the parameter is present (including when the value is empty string), without any modification to BaseAPIParameter.
Non-string/non-numeric $_REQUEST values are handled gracefully (return null), and numeric values are converted to their string representation.
clearableString() factory method exists on ParamTypeSelector, returns ClearableStringParameter, and follows the same instantiate-register-return pattern as string().

ClearableStringParameterTest covers at minimum: absent key, empty string, whitespace-only string, valid string with leading/trailing whitespace, numeric value, non-string value, hasValue() for absent vs. present, and setMaxLength() integration.

comments.note: StringParameter::getValue() calls parent::getValue() twice when the value is a string (line 171-172: calls parent::getValue() to check type, then calls it again to return). The result is cached so there's no functional impact, but the double call is misleading. Consider storing the result in a local variable instead.

BaseAPIParameter::hasValue() returns $this->getValue() !== null. For ClearableStringParameter this works correctly (empty string '' !== null → true), but the contract relies on an implicit assumption that empty-string is a valid non-null value. A brief doc comment on hasValue() explaining this distinction would help future maintainers avoid accidentally treating '' as absent.

[documentation-forward] BaseAPIParameter::hasValue() has no PHPDoc explaining that it returns true for empty-string values ('' !== null). For ClearableStringParameter callers, the distinction between hasValue()===false (absent) and getValue()==='' (cleared) is the core contract — a doc comment on hasValue() should call this out explicitly, ideally with a @see ClearableStringParameter cross-reference.

[documentation-forward] ClearableStringParameterTest::test_getTypeLabel_returnsClearableString() uses assertStringContainsString('learable', ...) — asserting a substring rather than the full label to tolerate translation. This pattern is non-obvious and a brief inline comment explaining why 'learable' (rather than 'Clearable string') is tested would help future maintainers avoid accidentally 'fixing' it.

notes: ClearableStringParameter is fully implemented and tested. The three-state semantic (null/empty-string/value) is driven by array_key_exists() on $_REQUEST — this is intentional and documented in the class PHPDoc.

setMaxLength() integration works naturally: MaxLengthValidation already skips empty strings and null, so clearable parameters that are 'cleared' (empty string) are never rejected by length validation.

The null-when-key-is-null edge case (key present in $_REQUEST with null value) produces a warning and returns null — this is consistent with how StringParameter handles non-string values. One test (test_nullValue_distinguishedFromAbsent_returnsNull) documents this behavior.
